title: Does the error of reconstructing a cut link depend on which link is cut, and on the separation across the gap?
question: Across every valid cut of real connected networks, does the random-baseline bridge's recovery error vary beyond sampling error, and is it predicted by population and design separation across the induced gap, measured from published summaries before recovery?
design: Four aggregate networks from multinma and netmeta; every treatment split that disconnects the network, bridged by exchangeable and covariate-adjusted random baselines and scored against the connected estimate; variance of z across cuts and slopes on separation against each network's own bridge-true null. 4 networks, 200 null and 100 positive-control replicates each.
